Prevention: Uproot and burn tomato stalks at end of season.
Plough the soil and leave free of crop for 3 months to expose the nematodes to dessication and death by heat before planting new crop.
Sow clean, certified, planting material from reliable sources (nematode-free - grown in uninfested soils)
Treat the seed beds with a fumigant before planting - see yellow column.
African marigold ( T. erecta ) at least two months before planting (tomatoes).
Use clean irrigation water, not muddy water.
Rotate tomatoes with cereal crops such as maize and sorghum in a 4 year rotation.
Crotalaria leaves 2 months after planting tomato seedlings.
The decomposing leaves release pesticidal chemicals.
Clean tools such as hoes with bleach or disinfectant after use, to prevent spread of nematodes.
Before planting tomato in a new area, send soil samples to the lab to check for presence of nematodes.
If water from boreholes is used for irrigation, this should be tested too.
Monitoring: Check for signs of root knot nematodes: yellowing of leaves, wilting of plants despite adequate moisture, stunting of plants, fruit deformation and drop.
New leaves appear distorted and crinkled along the margin.
Check for nematodes by digging up plants from several different areas of the field and check for galls on roots of affected plants.
When 20% of the sampled plants have galls, then direct control measures should be applied.
Galls formed on tomato roots by nematodes do not fall off upon touching.
Direct Control: There are few direct control methods for nematodes, the most effective control methods are preventative.
Use as a soil drench at 6-8ml/10m2 (6-8 litres/ha).
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink or smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
The seedbeds can be treated with a fumigant before the seedlings are sown to reduce the level of infection.
GR) at the rate of 4.5kg/30 m2 to the bed 2 weeks before sowing.
Broadcast on surface of soil and plough it in to incorporate the chemical along and across the bed to a depth of 30 cm, then cover with a fumigation plastic paper for two weeks.
Dazomet is a soil fumigant; the granuals turn into a gas that kills nematodes, fungi and insects.
This pesticide is toxic to fish and aquatic invertebrates.
It is highly soluable in water
